turns.speaker: N1
turns.text: Welcome to this IELTS-style Listening practice test. You will hear two people talking about their work at NASA. First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 6. Now listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 6.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Hi Mike, this is Sarah from the research department. I wanted to talk about your project on space propulsion systems.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Sure thing, Sarah. What do you need?

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: I’ve been looking at the proposal and it’s really well-written, but there are a few things I think we can improve.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Okay, let's go through them one by one. The first thing is that you mention using ion thrusters for propulsion, right?

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Yes, but there are some new advancements in solar sails that might be more efficient and cost-effective.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Hmm, I see. And the second point is about the timeline. You propose a launch date of 2035?

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Yes, but maybe we should consider pushing it back to 2040 to allow for more time on testing and development.

turns.speaker: N1
turns.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 7 to 10. Now listen carefully and answer questions 7 to 10.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Lastly, I wanted to discuss the funding. The proposal states that we have $3 million for this project.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Yes, but in reality, NASA only allocated $2.5 million. We need to find a way to secure additional funds.
